whatItFakes: The share of adults with a bachelor's degree (school.college-completion-pct) stays the web's ledger number (base times the links' factors); no engine decides who completes college. The state's higher education line reaches it only there: higher-education-spending-to-college-completion runs in the web on that line, and no engine reads its factor.
why: The measure is a stock of everyone 25 and older, and the core records no degrees or college enrollment on a person, so there is nothing for a student's June record to roll into; building it needs a college-going and degree record. The school engine (decideSchoolOutcome in src/core2/school-outcomes.ts) decides only a senior's graduation, and the jobs engine (schoolingOn in src/core2/modules/jobs.ts) holds every graduate at no college, so no engine decides a named graduate's completion.
replacement: A college engine that gives each graduate an enrollment and completion record by the same standing rule, and a degree on each adult, read back as this measure. That engine, at the moment it decides a graduate's completion, multiplies the graduate's own rate by webReach(api, placeId, "school.college-completion-pct", subject), which is how higher-education-spending-to-college-completion reaches a person; schoolingOn then reads the degree when it prices a hire.
resolution: Resolved by the college step in decideCollege (src/core2/school-outcomes.ts): on the day a senior year's graduation is decided, each graduate is ranked by the same standing, within their income fifth, for whether they enroll in college and, of those who enroll, whether they complete a bachelor's. The completion rate is the NCES six-year share (moved by the world's own factor) times webReach(api, placeId, "school.college-completion-pct", { incomeFifth }), which is how higher-education-spending-to-college-completion reaches a named graduate; the rate, factor and web month row are kept on the graduate's college record (the school module's college table). schoolingOn (src/core2/modules/jobs.ts) reads the record once normal time has ended, a bachelor's for a completer and some college for an enrolled graduate who does not complete, and prices the hire on it. The share of adults holding a degree is still the web's ledger (SG-SCHOOL-college-stock-ledger); the step is decided at graduation (SG-SCHOOL-college-decided-at-graduation). Proved by src/core2/law-wiring-college-step.test.ts.

whatItFakes: A graduate's college enrollment and bachelor's completion are both decided on the day the senior year's graduation is decided, at the national NCES shares (62 percent of completers enroll; 64 percent of first-time full-time starters at four-year schools finish in six years) spread over the income fifths by researched gradients, not year by year in college; the six-year share of four-year starters is applied to every enrolled graduate, two-year enrollees included; every completer holds the bachelor's at normal time (four years), though about a third take longer.
why: The core records nothing of a student's years in college (credits, tuition paid, terms, a school), so there is nothing for a later year's completion to read except the spending that was in force when the web's factor was read. The step is a background simulation the owner ruled for on Oct 29, 2026 (docs/coordination/OWNER-DECISIONS.md), not a step the player takes, so the smallest version is a decision at graduation with the record kept for the years after.
replacement: A completion decided in the spring each enrolled graduate's normal time ends (and later for those who take longer), ranked by the same standing and multiplied by the web's factor for school.college-completion-pct as it then stands, with the NCES shares for the starters at four-year schools and for the two-year enrollees each applied to their own, each in src/core2/data/school/outcomes.json.

whatItFakes: The share of adults with a bachelor's degree (school.college-completion-pct) stays the outcome web's ledger number (its 2024 base times the links' factors); the degrees the school engine decides for each graduating class are its yearly flow and are not summed into it.
why: The measure is a stock of every adult 25 and older, and the core holds degrees only for the graduates who finished a senior year in play: the adults who left school before the world opened carry the education record they were generated with, not a decided degree. Summing the two into one stock is the replacement of the ledger and is its own step (web-college-completion-stock-not-accumulated).
replacement: The measure read from the degrees: the share of a place's adults whose schoolingOn is a bachelor's, with the web's ledger keeping no copy of it (docs/pool/items/web-college-completion-stock-not-accumulated.md).

whatItFakes: The equalized-funding law's link into spending per student is the web's number; no law handler moves the schools budget line, so the school spending measure does not follow the law.
why: No handler in src/core2/law-reach moves the education budget for education.equalize-school-funding (law handlers belong to the law-wiring area).
replacement: A law-reach handler that moves the schools line of the budget in force (moveBudget), which the school engine's spending measure then reads. The graduation effect of that spending then runs through school-spending-to-attainment (the schools line above its Census base), so equalized-funding-to-graduation, the reduced form of the same study through the law, is dropped in the same change.

whatItFakes: The share of public school students who are Hispanic (school.hispanic-enrollment) stays the web's ledger; no engine decides it, so the enforcement link into it (enforcement-to-hispanic-enrollment, which runs in the web on the 287(g) partnership law) moves only that number.
why: The core records no ethnicity on a student (neither a full person nor a counted household) and no enrollment by ethnicity: the school engine (schoolFor in src/core2/modules/school.ts) sends every school-age person to the town's one district, so enrollment is never decided, only attendance, and there is nothing for the link to change.
replacement: An enrollment record by ethnicity (from the opening's school enrollment, src/core2/opening-public-schools.ts) that the school engine decides, with a student's ethnicity from the opening's population counts; at the moment it decides whether a student stays enrolled it multiplies the student's own rate by webReach(api, placeId, "school.hispanic-enrollment", subject), which is how enforcement-to-hispanic-enrollment (-0.10 after 24 months, Dee and Murphy 2020) changes who stays enrolled, read back as this measure.

whatItFakes: Seven researched links into school outcomes do not run, each because its cause is not recorded: class-size-to-scores (no K-3 class size), police-killing-to-graduation (no police killing, and the effect is for students who live near one), daca-to-graduation (no deferred action; a student's immigration status is seeded at both tiers, isUnauthorized in src/core2/citizenship.ts, but children take the adult citizen share), homicide-nearby-to-scores (no homicide below the place, and the effect is for a child tested right after one on their block), lead-to-reading (no blood lead), heat-to-learning (no school-year temperature) and carbon-monoxide-to-absence (no carbon monoxide). school-move-to-scores is no longer one of them: the school engine reads a student's own move (stopgap SG-SCHOOL-switch-window). Family income reaches only math: family-income-to-scores is carried by poverty-to-math-proficiency, and nothing moves reading proficiency by family income.
why: Each needs a cause or a per-student exposure record the core does not keep; the school engine reads only links that run or are carried. The engine that would read each once its cause is recorded: decideSchoolOutcome in src/core2/school-outcomes.ts for class-size-to-scores (the grade 8 math and reading tests, from a K-3 roster, which the school engine does not hold because a town has one district and no classrooms), homicide-nearby-to-scores (the testing day, from a homicide record with a block group), lead-to-reading (the reading test, from a child's blood lead record; the effect is on the share far below proficient, which the engine does not decide and the research does not convert to the proficient share), police-killing-to-graduation and daca-to-graduation (the senior's graduation, from a killing record near the student's home and from a deferred-action record read with the student's own immigration status (isUnauthorized in src/core2/citizenship.ts), whose research sizes are not set); schoolDay in src/core2/modules/school.ts for carbon-monoxide-to-absence (a student's daily choice to attend, from a carbon monoxide reading; the study's effect is a threshold on daily readings with no size the game can apply); and no engine at all for heat-to-learning (school.learning: the engine decides proficiency and graduation, not a year's learning). The other links in the family are settled: school-spending-to-attainment runs on the schools budget line, prek-to-graduation, child-coverage-to-graduation and family-income-to-scores are carried by built links from the same studies, and home-internet-to-scores and tuition-freeze-to-college-completion are about zero in the research.
replacement: Record each cause (class size, blood lead, school-year heat, carbon monoxide, a police killing or homicide with a place below the town, deferred action, with a child's own noncitizen share for student status) or a per-student exposure record, size the link from its study in the engine's units (for a standard-deviation effect on a proficiency share, the normal-density conversion at the base share as school-move-to-scores does), and read it where the engine named above decides, as the school-move read in decideSchoolOutcome does. A reading link from family income needs the poverty-to-math-proficiency per-point size confirmed first.

whatItFakes: A student's school switch (school-move-to-scores) is a household that moved into the town after the school year began (a counted-moves record, direction in, dated after September 1 and by the testing day), and every such move costs the average the study reports whatever its distance or timing. The cost to classmates who did not move, which the study also finds, is not applied, and a move inside the town, which keeps the town's one district, is not a switch.
why: The core has one school district per town (schoolFor in src/core2/modules/school.ts), so the only record of a student changing schools is a household arriving (src/core2/modules/counted-moves.ts). Hanushek, Kain and Rivkin 2004 (Table 2) find no significant extra cost for a move inside the school year and about none for a move across regions, so the average is the stated size with the study's preferred, smaller estimate as the low end of its range; the classmates' turnover cost needs the share of new students in each school, which no record keeps below the town.
replacement: Schools below the town (a district's campuses), so a move between campuses of one district is a switch too and each school's share of new students is a record; then the classmates' turnover cost (0.013 standard deviations for a one standard deviation rise in the share of new students) and the move's distance and timing are read where decideSchoolOutcome decides the grade 8 math test.

whatItFakes: A counted student's attendance in the school standing, and a full student's before they have an attendance record, is the mean attendance share of the same place's full students of that grade, or every school day where the place has none recorded. The standing orders who in an income fifth passes or graduates; it never sets how many do.
why: Only full people go to school day by day (school.ts records their days); a counted student has no attendance record. Today every full student attends every school day (SG-CORE-school-days), so the place's mean is every day and both tiers read the same value.
replacement: Counted students' attendance from the counted tier's own school days (the same attendance choice full students make, read for the group times its count), so the standing reads one recorded rule in both tiers.

whatItFakes: The cause of school-spending-to-attainment is the schools line of the town's city and county budgets above its Census base, standing for the study's change in per-pupil spending. It equals that change only while enrollment stays at the base the line was drawn for: enrollment growth that outruns the line, which lowers spending per student, does not register.
why: The Census base lines scale with the government's residents at the opening and the school engine's per-student spending (recordSchoolSpending) is not a base-relative series the web can read, so the budget line is the one recorded cause of school money that a mayor or council changes.
replacement: The school engine's spending per enrolled student as the cause, measured against its first reading, once the schools line follows enrollment (and the equalized-funding law moves it), so students leaving or arriving change spending per student as the study's treatment does.

whatItFakes: Every place opens owing no school honors: each place's remainder (the fraction of a spelling-bee or Division I signing its students were expected to earn) starts at zero on the day the world opens, though the years before the start would have left each place somewhere between zero and one.
why: The school years before the start (schoolHistory in past-school.ts) record where each person went to school but decide no honors, so there is no past remainder to read. The effect is that a small town's first honor comes about as many years after the start as it takes its expected counts to add up to one student, and a large town's comes in the first year.
replacement: The school years before the start run the honors (the same rule, each past year's students and rate) so every place opens with the remainder its past leaves it.

whatItFakes: Which seniors sign to play at a Division I school is ranked by the school standing plus three personality traits (competitive, persistent, voluntary effort), because no record in the world gives a student's athletic ability, teams or sports. The traits only rank the seniors; the count comes from the NCAA rate and the place's students.
why: No engine keeps a fitness, sport or team record for a student, and the health engine keeps conditions and strain, not fitness. Competing against others, sticking with practice and effort no one requires are the closest recorded traits.
replacement: A student's sports and athletic ability as a record (a body and fitness record that grows with practice, and school teams with rosters), read by the honors in place of the traits, which then only break ties.

whatItFakes: Every Division I signing of a senior class is decided on one day, the first Wednesday of December (the football early signing period), though the signings fall across the early period, the first Wednesday of February and the other sports' November and April periods.
why: The research found the football dates (ESPN, Dec 3, 2025 and Feb 4, 2026) but no source for the share of a class that signs in each period, and a share would be a typed number.
replacement: One row per signing period in honors.json, each with the share of the year's Division I signings that fall in it, from NCAA signing-period data.

whatItFakes: Every place with students in grades 5 to 8 holds a spelling bee each year and crowns one winner, though not every school or district enrolls in the Scripps program, and a real place has several schools whose champions meet in a district or county bee.
why: The core keeps one school district per place (schoolFor in src/core2/modules/school.ts) and no record of which districts enroll in a spelling bee program; Scripps publishes the 10 million students who start a bee (spellingbee.com) but not the enrolled schools or districts.
replacement: The district's enrollment in the bee program as a record, a bee in each enrolled school and a district or county bee among their champions, so a place without a bee crowns no one and a place with several schools crowns several.
